Alejandro —

Thanks for the heads up. We can provide a compact evidence packet and an attestation letter. High-level summary (we'll attach the export and a signed appendix):

Scan cadence (production):
- Authenticated network & host scans: weekly (credentialed scan of core infra and customer-facing services).
- Unauthenticated external scanning: daily routine sweeps for internet-facing endpoints.
- Container image scanning: per-build (blocking for critical/high findings) with nightly re-scan of image registry.
- Dependency SCA: continuous with weekly aggregated reports.
- Third-party penetration test: annual + ad-hoc for major releases.

Remediation SLA (default commitments):
- Critical (CVSS 9.0–10.0 or equivalent exploitability): target 14 calendar days to remediation or documented compensating control; emergency hotfix can be deployed in 72 hours when there is confirmed exploitation.
- High (CVSS 7.0–8.9): target 30 calendar days to remediation or compensating control.
- Medium (CVSS 4.0–6.9): target 90 calendar days.
- Low (CVSS 0.1–3.9): target 180 calendar days or tracked backlog.

Notes on hosted vs private: for Hosted (Redwood API) our standard remediation practice above applies and is included in customer-facing evidence. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers may elect to operate their own patch cadence; in those cases we provide scan exports and recommended SLA language but cannot guarantee patch push timelines without a Dedicated contract addendum.

Attachments included in this message:
- vm-scan-index-202611.zip (index of authenticated/unauthed scan exports; CSV manifest inside)
- cve-commitment-matrix.xlsx (mapping of active CVEs, detection date, owner, remediation ETA)
- scan-cadence-diagram.png (visual of cadence and escalation flow)
- sig-evidence-appendix.pdf (signed attestation and short narrative for SIG intake)

I'll also open an internal ticket (JIRA-SEC-4879) and ask Kimberly to provide a short attestation note on exceptions and compensating controls. Expect the formal packet uploaded to the shared drive by EOD 2026-11-13.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Alejandro / Soojin —

Adding a technical attestation and a short exceptions policy summary. Key points for assessors to note:

1) Ownership and verification
- Each CVE is assigned a remediation owner within Infra/Platform or Product. Ownership is visible in the ticketing payload and the cve-commitment-matrix.xlsx we attached.

2) Exception & compensating control policy
- When a remediation requires > SLA window (e.g., unacceptable risk of regression or complex vendor dependency), the owner must document: mitigation steps (WAF rule, config hardening, traffic isolation), risk acceptance justification, and an explicit re-evaluation date (no > 90 days without leadership review).

3) Evidence exemplar
- In the zip manifest we included: authenticated_scan_2026-09-28.csv (sample), remediation_ticket_SEC-1402.eml (redacted), and pipeline-blocking logs for an image CVE where we applied image rebuild and redeploy.

4) Hosted customer guarantees
- For hosted customers we operate under the remediation cadence above; we will notify customers via the Console incident page and send token-level cost/latency attribution if a remediation requires a rolling canary.

If you want, I can prepare a one-page technical addendum that the SIG assessor can use as a quick reference.

Kimberly Park
